description: Shelter topic and core cards added in Library content 1.4.0. Each card was checked against the cited official pages on 2026-11-04; page_last_updated is the date each page showed when read. Household wording and sequencing are HomePrep editorial applications.

evidence.title: Tornadoes
evidence.locator: Before a Tornado; During a Tornado; If You Are Under A Tornado or Severe Weather Warning
evidence.support_scope: Safe room or ICC 500 storm shelter; next best a small, interior, windowless room or basement on the lowest level of a sturdy building; stay away from windows, doors and outside walls; go to a public shelter if you can't stay at home.

evidence.title: Floods
evidence.locator: If you are under a flood warning; During a Flood
evidence.support_scope: Depending on the type of flooding: evacuate if told to, move to higher ground or a higher floor, or stay where you are; evacuate immediately if told to; never drive around barricades; don't walk, swim or drive through flood waters; if trapped in a building go to the highest level, not a closed attic.

evidence.title: Shelter
evidence.locator: Introduction; Mass Care Shelter; Sheltering in Place
evidence.support_scope: Stay informed and follow local authorities; shelter in place when there is a lot of debris in the air or authorities say the air is badly contaminated; take your emergency supply kit; all shelters accept service animals but many public shelters and hotels do not allow pets; text SHELTER and your ZIP code to 43362 to find open shelters.

evidence.title: Evacuation
evidence.locator: Know When and Where to Go; Before, During and After an Evacuation
evidence.support_scope: Follow the instructions of local officials; know your destination; identify several places in different directions; alternate routes and transportation, including without a car; leave early enough to avoid being trapped; follow recommended routes; don't drive into flooded areas; check on neighbors who may need a ride; check with officials before returning.

evidence.title: People with Disabilities
evidence.support_scope: Plan accessible transportation for evacuation with local transit and emergency management; voluntary registries kept by local emergency management; a support network and contact list; plan how to evacuate with assistive devices; know whether a shelter allows pets or only service animals.

cards.title: Choose where to shelter for each hazard
cards.when_to_use: Before a warning, for each hazard that can affect your home
prerequisites: Know which hazards, such as tornadoes or floods, can affect where you live
steps: Tornado or severe wind warning: go to a safe room or storm shelter if you have one. Otherwise use a small, interior, windowless room or basement on the lowest level of a sturdy building, away from windows, doors and outside walls.
Flood warning: depending on the type of flooding, evacuate if told to, move to higher ground or a higher floor, or stay where you are. Don’t plan to shelter on a level that may flood.
If rising water traps you in a building, go to the highest level. Don’t climb into a closed attic; get on the roof only if necessary, and signal for help.
Shelter in place (stay inside where you are) when local authorities say the outside air is badly contaminated, or there is a lot of debris in the air.
Record the location you chose for each hazard and practice going there.
limits: The safest place depends on the hazard: a basement suited to a tornado can be the wrong place in a flood.
If your home has no suitable place, know a public shelter or sturdy building you can reach in time.
Current instructions from local authorities come before this plan.

evidence.scope: Tornado shelter choices and what to stay away from.
Flood options depend on the type of flooding; highest level, not a closed attic, if trapped.
When sheltering in place applies, and following local authorities.

completion: Record a shelter location for each hazard that applies to your home and confirm everyone knows it.
cards.maintenance: Review after a move, a renovation, or learning of a new local hazard.
cards.escalation: Follow local warnings and official instructions. Call 911 if you are trapped or in immediate danger.

cards.title: Arrange an accessible backup place to stay
cards.when_to_use: Before you may need to leave home
prerequisites: Each household member’s mobility, medical, equipment and animal needs
steps: Identify several places you could go, such as a friend’s or relative’s home in another town or a motel, in different directions.

Check that each place works for everyone: access for anyone with a mobility need, room for assistive devices and medical equipment, and whether pets are allowed. All shelters accept service animals, but many public shelters and hotels don’t allow pets.
Plan accessible transportation if anyone needs it, including how you’d leave without a car. Check options with local transit providers and your emergency management agency.
Ask your local emergency management office whether it keeps a voluntary registry for people with disabilities.
Share the plan with your support network and keep their contact list with your emergency kit.
limits: Public shelter spaces can change: check with local officials each year.
A destination isn’t usable if it’s in the affected area or the route to it is unsafe.

evidence.scope: Several destinations in different directions, and transportation without a car.
Accessible transportation, voluntary registries, support network and assistive devices.
Service animals and pets at shelters, and finding open shelters.

completion: Record at least two destinations in different directions and how each person will get there, and confirm each meets your household’s access needs.
cards.maintenance: Recheck each year, and when someone’s needs, your transportation or a host’s situation changes.
cards.escalation: If no planned destination is available, find an open shelter by texting SHELTER and your ZIP code to 43362 (standard rates apply), or follow local officials.

cards.title: Follow official evacuation instructions
cards.when_to_use: When a hazard threatens your area
prerequisites: A way to receive local alerts and instructions
steps: Follow the instructions of local officials, and evacuate when they tell you to. In a flood, evacuate immediately if told to.
Leave early enough to avoid being trapped by severe weather.
Follow recommended evacuation routes; shortcuts may be blocked. Depending on the disaster, your route may be on foot.
Don’t walk or drive into flooded areas or around barricades, and watch for washed-out roads or bridges and downed power lines.
Take your emergency supply kit and your pets, and check on neighbors who may need a ride.
Before going home, check with local officials both where you’re staying and back home.
limits: Officials may tell you to stay where you are instead of leaving; follow the instruction for the hazard you face.
Only service animals may be allowed in public shelters.

evidence.scope: Following local officials, leaving early, routes, road hazards, neighbors and returning home.
Evacuate immediately if told to; never drive around barricades or through flood waters.

completion: Confirm how you’ll receive evacuation instructions and that everyone knows the plan for leaving.
cards.maintenance: Review before seasonal hazards and when your routes or destinations change.
cards.escalation: Call 911 if you are trapped or in immediate danger.
